figures.finding: Zambia's Employment Code bars employing a child in a covered work site, allows light work from thirteen to fifteen that harms neither health nor schooling, and excepts a child's participation in artistic performances done under a statutory instrument the Minister issues setting the hours and conditions.

value.permit: statutory instrument by the Minister (hours, conditions), s. 82(3)(a)
value.reachesWritingDirecting: no: the exception is for participation in artistic performances

figures.applies: Zambia, Employment Code Act 2019 s. 82. Whether the Minister has issued the statutory instrument was not found.

sources.said: a person shall not employ a child in a covered work site. (2) Despite subsection (1), a child aged between thirteen and fifteen years may be engaged in light work

Subsection (1) shall not apply to— (a) work constituting the participation of the child in artistic performances in accordance with a statutory instrument, issued by the Minister, prescribing— (i) the number of hours to be worked; (ii) the conditions in which the work may be undertaken

figures.finding: A company appoints a natural person as director, and no one under eighteen may be appointed.
figures.applies: Zambia, Companies Act, 2017 (Act No. 10 of 2017), s. 92(1) and (3)(a), the National Assembly's copy.

sources.said: Qualifications of director 92. (1) A company shall appoint a natural person as director. (2) A director may not be a member or hold shares in the company, unless the articles provide otherwise. (3) A person shall not be appointed as a director if that person— (a) is under eighteen years of age; (b) is an undischarged bankrupt; (c) is disqualified by section 93 from being a director;
